summary.tldr: Requires Veterans Affairs to create and publish a framework for animal-assisted services for veterans, then review it later.
what_it_does: Requires the Minister of Veterans Affairs to work with service providers and departmental advisory groups to develop and carry out a framework for animal-assisted services to veterans.
Requires the framework to set processes and standards, including what documents Veterans Affairs may ask for when a veteran requests these services.
Requires the framework to include third-party accreditation requirements, ways to check provider compliance, and clear goals, timelines, and monitoring measures.
Requires the Minister to table a report on the framework in Parliament within 12 months of the law coming into force and to publish it on the department’s website.
Requires an independent review of the framework five years after the report is tabled, with the review report also tabled and published.
summary.background: The bill defines animal-assisted service to include trained assistance animals and animal-assisted interventions, including activities and therapy. It says the Minister must consider a 2022 House of Commons veterans committee report on service dogs.
